definitions.explanation: A physics term for the pulling force transmitted along a string, rope, or surface, or the force resisting being stretched.

examples.japanese: ロープに{張力|ちょうりょく}がかかる。
examples.english: Tension is applied to the rope.

examples.japanese: {水|みず}の{表面|ひょうめん}{張力|ちょうりょく}で{虫|むし}が{浮|う}いている。
examples.english: The insect floats thanks to the surface tension of the water.

examples.japanese: {糸|いと}にかかる{張力|ちょうりょく}が{大|おお}きすぎると、{糸|いと}は{切|き}れてしまう。
examples.english: If the tension on the thread is too great, the thread will snap.

notes:
Compound of {張|ちょう} (stretch, pull taut) + {力|りょく} (force). A technical term used mainly in physics and engineering.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {表面|ひょうめん}{張力|ちょうりょく}: surface tension
- {張力|ちょうりょく}がかかる: tension is applied
- {張力|ちょうりょく}を{加|くわ}える: to apply tensile force

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {引力|いんりょく}: attractive force; gravitation — pulls objects together, not a force along a string
- {圧力|あつりょく}: pressure — a pushing force per unit area, the opposite kind of stress
